questions.question: What numbers does list(range(4)) produce?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! range(n) starts at 0 and stops right before n.

questions.question: How do you generate numbers from 5 to 10 inclusive in Python?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Since range stops before the end value, range(5, 11) includes 10.
questions.explanation_incorrect: To include 10, the stop parameter must be 11: range(5, 11).

questions.question: What does the third argument in range(0, 10, 2) represent?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! The third argument specifies how much to jump each iteration.
questions.explanation_incorrect: range(start, stop, step) uses the 3rd argument as the step increment.

questions.explanation_correct: Correct! range(5) produces 5 values (0, 1, 2, 3, 4), so the body runs 5 times.
